key_insight: Abstracting QCCD trapped-ion hardware into architectural archetypes exposes distinct compilation challenges and makes hardware–compiler co-design essential.
engineering_relevance: Register layout and connectivity shape routing costs, so compiler requirements should inform QCCD hardware design.
method: Abstract QCCD architectures and native operations into compiler-ready models.
Organize the design space into archetypes and apply compilation methods to 1D and 2D architectures.
Extend compilation analysis to include a quantum error-correction layer.
evidence_signal: The compilation evaluation finds routing overhead scaling approximately cubically with qubit count in the studied 1D architecture and quadratically in the studied 2D architecture.
watch_item: These approximate scaling results should not be assumed universal across QCCD layouts or equivalent to end-to-end runtime and error performance.
paper_title: From QCCD Trapped-Ion Hardware to Quantum Compilers: Capabilities, Architectures, and Compilation
